hub.say: Pull up a stool. Drink's warm, company's warmer.

opts.t: Heard you have a hound problem.

hounds.say: Mutant hounds north of town, at the old Dens. Five of them at least. Kill five and I'll make it worth your time.

houndsdone.say: You actually did it! Drinks are on me for a week.

brother.say: My brother Tomas. He went scavenging at the Collapsed Depot nine days back, with our mother's locket for luck. It's east, off the Bunker road. If you're headed that way... just look. Please.

tomas.say: That's... that's Ma's locket. Where did you get that?

truth.say: ...I knew. Nine days, I knew. Thank you for not making me keep wondering. I'll bring him home. You eat free here, and the bed's yours whenever you want it.

lie.say: East! That idiot. That beautiful idiot. He always said he'd see the coast. Here, take this, it's what I'd saved to pay a search party.

rumor.say: They say Kess keeps her loot under a very paranoid lock. People in hoods at the Burned Chapel carry lanterns in daylight. Hollis Grange out west lost half his herd to a boar the size of a car. And somebody saw a dog sitting by the Collapsed Depot, just waiting. Oh, and there's a casino on the Gantry road now, the Silver Spur. Lou runs a straight table there, they say.

cr.say: Just one. This goes to Oskar Vane in Saltreach. It's sealed, and it stays sealed. Fifty chits on delivery, and a drink on the house when you're back.

wrc.say: Ines sent you? Fine. Dustwell dug the first wells into that aquifer forty years ago, with our hands. Saltreach just sits on top of it and calls it theirs. We'd share. We just won't be told.

dh.say: I want a house special. Something that glows in the glass. Three clean waters and two glow fungus and I'll do the rest. Mostly safe. Mostly.

dhdone.say: Watch. ...See that? Glows. Doesn't bite, much. First two are on the house. Well, they're yours. Don't drink them both at once.

scrap.say: Eight scrap metal, three circuit boards. Ruins and wrecks are full of both. Bring them and I'll make it worth your while, and I'll open the good shelf for you.

scrapdone.say: Beautiful! Clean, no rust rot. Here's your cut. Have a look at the stock again, I've put the caravan goods out.

prices.say: Every trader pays more for what they deal in: I like junk, Brannock likes iron, the Doc likes medicine. We all restock at sunrise, and none of us has bottomless pockets. Do right by the town and we shave the price. Charm doesn't hurt either.

debt.say: Three hundred? I haven't SEEN three hundred since before the bombs. Please, I've got stock to buy, I've got...

debtthreat.say: All right! All right. Here. That's the till and my lucky coin. Happy?

debtpaid.say: You... you'd do that? I'll pay you back. Some of it. Most of it. I'll try.

debtdeal.say: Fifty a week? I can do fifty a week. I can almost do fifty a week. Thank you, friend.

hub.say: Brannock. If it shoots, I fix it. If it doesn't shoot, I fix that too.

tools.say: Raiders hit my wagon up on the north ridge, east of the reactor road. Took my tool roll. Forty years of files and reamers. Bring it back and I'll put something special in your hand.

toolsdone.say: Every one of them still in its loop. Ha! Here. I built this for myself and never had the nerve to carry it. She's called Promise.

advice.say: Workbench is behind me. Tune a gun three times and it's a different gun, but you'll need gears past the first. Aim down the barrel and stop moving. And a revolver doesn't jam, which is more than I can say for people.

buggy.say: The Rust Runner. Raced her on the salt flats before the war took the salt. Bring me three gears, five scrap and two circuits, and she's yours. I'm too old to drive anything faster than a grudge.

buggydone.say: Give me an hour... There. She coughs, she rattles and she'll do ninety downhill. Key's yours. Try not to hit anyone you like.

bc.say: Cinder Quarry has a storehouse full of blasting powder the raiders don't know how to use. I know how to use it. Bring me a crate and I'll turn some of it into something useful for you.

bcdone.say: Careful, careful... lovely. Three pipe bombs, fresh off the bench, and some chits. Don't throw them indoors.

sd.say: Ten good lumps of scrap and four gears that turn. What for? A surprise. A loud one. Pays well.

sddone.say: Beautiful. Every one of them. Here. And when you hear a very large noise from Dustwell next month, you didn't hear it from me.

thanks.say: Bless you. There's still people out here, then. Not just guns walking around with legs.

scorn.say: Mm. The wastes make some folk hard. Mind it doesn't make you empty.

done.say: You've done enough today, dear. Come by tomorrow and I'll tell you about the war. I was very young.

tt.say: Thaddeus played the harmonica every night. Badly. I would give anything to hear it again, even badly. We left it in the eastern ruins, in the house with the blue door, when the dogs came.

ttdone.say: Oh... oh, it still smells like him. Tobacco and tin. I can't play a note. I don't care. Take these, child. You gave an old woman back her evenings.

hub.say: Don't touch the antenna! ...oh. Hello. I'm Wick. I'm making this old relay talk again.

log.say: Cold-start? ...Oh. Oh no. Two winters ago, 03:12. It didn't originate here, I only relayed it. It came up the old highway line from the roadside emergency terminal at the Dry Overpass, east of Gantry. Whoever typed it signed it. Go and read it.

need.say: Three fusion cells. There's one in each of three ruins: the Collapsed Depot, the Burned Chapel, and the Dry Overpass. Bring them to the terminal here and I'll boot it. Then I can sell you things that hum.

status.say: Cells in the terminal over there, please. I'm vibrating.

drones.say: Meridian security drones! Three of them, circling the dish and zapping anything that hums, including me. Their logic cores are worth a lot to me, if you bring any back.

opts.t: I'll knock them out of the sky.

dronesdone.say: The dish is singing again! Here, cells for the trouble, and I'll pay top chits for any logic cores you find.

bb.say: There's one thing. The last relief plane out of Kestrel Airfield came back without its pilot. The flight recorder's still in Hangar 2. I want to hear it. I want to know what she saw up there.

bbdone.say: Let me... there. Static, then her voice. "Kestrel relief, engine two out, I'm putting down on the north flats." Then nothing. Captain Ruth Abara. She didn't come back with the plane because she wasn't in it. She bailed. North flats, past the airfield.

bo.say: With a booster on the overpass mast it can. Two circuits and two lengths of copper, wired into the junction box at the top of the ramp. Then Saltreach can hear us, and we can hear them complain.

bodone.say: There it is. Saltreach on channel nine, loud and clear, already complaining. Here, cells, and my eternal professional respect.

intro.say: The dog lies beside the remains with its ribs showing. It lifts its head and growls, low and tired, but it does not get up.

joined.say: The dog eats like it has not in days, then sniffs your hand and gets up beside you. The tag on its collar is stamped BISCUIT.

party.say: Biscuit sits, tail sweeping the dust, waiting for you to decide.

intro.say: Easy. You've come a long way to stand in a burned church. ...You read the terminal, then. Rosalind Castellan. My grandmother ran Meridian's night shift. I sent the command.

why.say: I gave this valley power. For one winter Dustwell had heat and the children stopped dying of cold. Then the coolant regulator failed and the leak began. The thing that used to be Chief Engineer Abbott killed two of mine before we got the chamber sealed. He still carries the replacement part.

opts.t: So what now? Fix it, or kill it?

plan.say: Kill the core and the wells clear, and we go back to burning furniture. Fit the new regulator and it runs clean for a hundred years. Lights. Pumps. A purifier that works. I have a keycard. What I don't have is someone who can walk past Abbott.

hub.say: The lamp stays lit. What do you need?

sworn.say: Then take it. At the control terminal, install the regulator. Do not pull the scram lever. I am trusting you with the only future I've got.

honest.say: ...At least you're honest. Take it. Just look at Dustwell's dark windows on your way north, before you choose.

refuse.say: Then find another way in. Halloran keeps a spare, and he's too frightened to use it himself.

haven.say: Then open your door and come up here, where it's needed. One part can't save a hole in the ground and a whole valley both. I'm sorry. That's the arithmetic.

lamp.say: Engineers' grandchildren, mostly. We kept the manuals when everyone else burned them for warmth. We carry a light in the daytime so nobody forgets what one looks like.

thanks.say: I saw the tower beacon change colour from here. I didn't believe it until the chapel bulb came on. A hundred years, vault-born. You gave them a hundred years.

tusker.say: Boar the size of a car. Scarred up like a road map. Comes down from the hills west of the Relay Tower and takes a calf a week. Kill it and bring me three hides as proof, and you'll eat for a month.

paid.say: Ha! That's him, all right. Here, steaks and chits. And you're welcome at my fire any night.

life.say: Oxen don't care about the end of the world. They want grass, water and somebody to stand between them and the teeth. Simple. I like simple.

ru.say: Rustlers took two of my oxen last night. Tracks lead north-west, toward the hills above Haven 12. Three of them, maybe. I want my animals back more than I want them dead, but I'm not fussy.

rudone.say: Both girls walked home on their own this morning, chewing like nothing happened. Here. Steaks from a different ox, don't worry. And chits.

seeds.say: Seeds? Bean, squash, maize, and some tomato from my greenhouse. Here. Tell your vault people to talk to the plants. They like it.

os.say: Old Scar. A stalker the size of a cart horse, ear torn half off. Comes down from the hills north-east of the Hound Dens and takes an ox a week. Kill it and I'll pay what I've got.

osdone.say: Lord, look at the size of it. I'll sleep tonight for the first time in a month. Here, chits, and hides from the boars. You earned every one.

hub.say: The glow in the hills is getting brighter. My goats won't go near it. Smart goats.

more.say: I trade jerky for stories. You got a story? No? Then I've got jerky, at full price. Rook's a good mayor. Hard, but good. The good ones are always hard out here.

story.say: I ran water before I ran cards. Water makes you enemies. Cards make you friends who owe you money. I prefer the second kind.

rules.say: Blackjack pays three to two and the dealer stands on seventeen. The wheel has one green zero. The machines pay what they pay. Win too much and Knuckles walks you to the door, with a smile.

chip.say: Ah. So you're the curious kind. That little chip keeps the lights on, sweetheart. Three hundred chits says you put it back and forget you ever saw it.

bribed.say: A pleasure doing business. Drinks are on the house tonight. Only the drinks.

honest.say: ...You drive a hard bargain. Fine. The machines go honest and I tell everyone it was my idea. Here, for your trouble, and your silence about the last three years.

vip.say: High-roller chips and the big limits. Five hundred chits for the marker, and you keep it for life. The house likes its whales well fed.

vipfree.say: Since you were so... civilized about Old Patsy. Take it. A gift. Gifts are the house's most profitable investment.

vipyes.say: Welcome to the gold tables, darling. Chips up to five hundred, and the wheel takes two thousand a spin.

pd.say: Pocket Duggan owes the house three hundred chits and keeps sending me apologies instead. Collect it. How is your business.

history.say: Six years. I poured at the Dry Hole in Dustwell before that. Vex offered me double and a door that locks. In this valley a door that locks is worth more than double.

sour.say: Cactus juice, lime from Hollis's greenhouse, a splash of something Brannock distills, and a pinch of salt for the tears of the house. Mostly it's the salt.

patsy.say: Old Patsy. The machine by the bar. Three years, no jackpot. People feed it their water money. Get a look inside her, would you? There's a service panel round the back, if you're good with your hands.

chip.say: A governor. I knew it. Vex will pay you to keep quiet, or you can rip it out and let everybody win fair. Or you could flash that thing for yourself. I won't pretend I didn't think about that.

fair.say: Here. A hundred chits from my own tip jar, and I'd pay double. Vex will figure it out, but she can't prove it was you.

mine.say: Huh. Well. Just don't empty her in one night, or Knuckles will notice. I never saw a thing.

lucky.say: Walked out of the Meridian blast zone with all my fingers. Been gambling on borrowed time ever since. Seems a shame to stop now.

tips.say: Blackjack, stand on twelve when I show a six or less. Never take insurance. On the dice, the pass line is the friendliest bet in the house. And the wheel? The wheel is for people who like watching their money spin before it leaves.

hr.say: Ha! Alright. Walk out of here a thousand chits ahead in one night and I'll pay you two-fifty out of my own pocket. Lose, and you buy the next round for the whole room.

hrdone.say: A thousand up. You lucky so-and-so. Two-fifty, as promised. Now get out before Vex notices you exist.

night.say: Two fights, one proposal, a guy who tried to pay with a pre-war toaster. Toaster worked, though.
